newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat seen one to two cents lower on harvest.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat seen one to two cents lower on harvest.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures were expected to open one to two cents per bushel lower, under pressure from harvest acitivity in the U.S. southern Plains, traders said.
"The harvest is going to keep any rally in wheat from being too big," said one commission house trader.
Heavy rains and saturated soils in the eastern Corn Belt have generated some concerns over the quality of the soft red winter wheat crop, and those worries should support prices, traders said.
Slight weakness in overnight wheat values was also expected to spur additional selling on the open, traders said.
In overnight trade, wheat settled 1/2 to 1/4 cent lower.
